title: İskender Kebab
description: A legendary Bursa specialty featuring thinly sliced seasoned lamb and beef over toasted pide, rich tomato sauce, silky garlic yogurt, and sizzling browned butter.

instruction.title: Marinate the Meat
steps: Combine onion, garlic, olive oil, cumin, paprika, black pepper, and salt.
Coat the sliced meat thoroughly with the marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.

instruction.title: Prepare the Tomato Sauce
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add passata and water and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes.
Reduce until glossy and concentrated, then season to taste.
Keep warm.

instruction.title: Cook the Kebab
steps: Heat a heavy skillet or grill plate until extremely hot.
Cook the meat in small batches to prevent steaming.
Sear until deeply caramelized while keeping the center tender.
Rest briefly before slicing into serving pieces.

instruction.title: Assemble
steps: Cut the pide into small pieces and toast lightly.
Arrange the warm pide across a heated serving plate.
Spoon tomato sauce over the bread.
Arrange the hot kebab meat on top.
Add garlic yogurt beside the meat.
Pour additional tomato sauce over the kebab.
Brown the butter until fragrant and lightly golden.
Pour the sizzling butter over the meat immediately before serving.
Finish with grilled peppers, tomatoes, and parsley.

servingSuggestions.title: Restaurant-Style Presentation
items: Serve on a preheated wide ceramic plate.
Keep yogurt separate from the hot tomato sauce.
Pour browned butter tableside immediately before serving.
Serve with blistered green peppers and roasted tomatoes.
Use freshly toasted pide so it absorbs the sauce without becoming soggy.

chefTips: Partially freeze the meat for 20 to 30 minutes before slicing for ultra-thin pieces.
Never overcrowd the pan when searing.
The tomato sauce should be intense, glossy, and slightly acidic.
Use thick strained yogurt for a luxurious texture.
Brown the butter gently; burnt butter will overpower the dish.
Warm the plates before assembly to maintain the restaurant-quality presentation.
